title: fix: list ChatGPT models with a Codex client version
body:
Related: #201130, #201493

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT subscription model discovery sends OpenClaw's calendar version to a Codex-maintained API. The backend's client-version gates therefore receive a version from the wrong release stream.

## User Impact

Subscription discovery reports a stable Codex client version independently of OpenClaw releases. The first discovery after cache expiry can wait up to one second for npm; a registry failure still allows discovery using the bundled Codex version.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve npm's latest stable `@openai/codex` version, cache successful lookups for six hours, and use bundled Codex `0.169.0` as both the minimum and registry-failure fallback. Failed lookups are retried on the next discovery attempt. Responses attribution and Codex binary selection/update behavior remain independent.

This removes the calendar-version/`99.0.0` selection and reuses the existing guarded HTTP transport and catalog cache. A contract test keeps the floor aligned with the bundled dependency; test planning schedules that contract for pin changes. The existing Responses wrapper fixture moves into its existing support module to satisfy the line-cap ratchet, with its assertions preserved.

## Evidence

- Regression tests failed on the original behavior: discovery used OpenClaw `2026.11.5` where the Codex version was expected. The corrected discovery and provider contracts pass.
- 132 focused tests passed across discovery, provider listing, auth ordering, prompt stability, and the bundled-version contract. After the fixture move, all 33 provider tests and all 8 token-sharing tests passed again.
- Targeted typecheck, extension/core/script lint, formatting, and commit-hook checks passed. Targeted planner routing was verified; the broad planner suites were not completed locally.
- Authenticated live proof through an isolated foreground Gateway: npm lookup HTTP 200; `/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.171.0` HTTP 200; 10 available models; a real OpenClaw-runtime turn returned `CODEX_DISCOVERY_OK`. Responses used `originator=openclaw` and `version=2026.11.5`. The test Gateway was stopped after validation.
- Local autoreview of the initial working-tree candidate based on `140e6bf92c820eb9d7592c285106b62668319d50` reported scoped-clean at P0–P2. This predates the unchanged fixture relocation and timeout repair. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its source checkout lacks dependencies and build output. Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed `5387637c75960f946bb212c6415e69172f953862` and found one P2: npm could consume the entire five-second discovery budget.
- Fixed that P2 by limiting npm to one second. A new regression through `runProviderCatalogWithTimeout` fails with the old five-second timeout and passes with the fix: a stalled registry falls back to bundled Codex and still publishes models from a healthy endpoint within the existing owner budget. All 40 provider-listing contracts and 10 discovery tests passed; the new regression passed again after lint/format cleanup. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and commit hooks passed. Hosted [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202284#issuecomment-7032128287) of `894480111d85fb03a5f907833e799370159af7fa` confirmed the timeout finding is resolved and reported no actionable findings.

Broad coverage remains with PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

Against the merge base: production +73/-14 lines; tests, fixtures, and planning +257/-76; docs and guide +11/-11. The new resolver contains the Codex version lookup, cache policy, and fallback; it adds no new cache or transport owner.

</details>
